audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent from every field. (a) Void Stone reduces magic damage and Galio's entire kit is magic. (b) Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage specifically, so it eats a Galio combo whole. (c) Null Sphere interrupts channels — it stops Hero's Entrance mid-channel.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage'; 'granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage'; 'dealing damage and interrupting channels.' Galio's R text is a designated landing with a delay — an interruptible channel. Together these decide whether a Galio commit is worth anything.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and packet.defects reported zero sequencing cues on the whole matchup.
audit.why: The punishable cooldown here is Force Pulse at 21s rank 1, not Riftwalk — Riftwalk is 5s and never truly down; the cost is mana, not time.
audit.corrected: Rewrote with Force Pulse 21s, Riftwalk 5s at rank 1 with escalating mana on recasts, and an explicit 'punish the second blink, not the first' sequencing line.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions carried a 'channel-interruptible' rule claiming Kassadin's Null Sphere is a channel your W or R cancels. It is not.
audit.why: Riot's Q text says Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels — the derived 'channel' flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire on that phrase. The interaction runs the other way: his Q interrupts YOUR channel.
audit.corrected: Did not write the false claim. Wrote the correct direction into breakdown.carry instead.

edits.before: AP assassins picked the wrong statue — taunt the dive, shield the burst, and watch the assassination become community service.
edits.after: Void Stone cuts your magic damage and Null Sphere shields the rest — taunt him off the wave early and close before Riftwalk stacks.

edits.before: Taunt the dive and let the shield do the arguing — AP assassins fund your lane. Riftwalk is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step forward.
edits.after: Shove him under tower while Force Pulse is 21 seconds and every extra Riftwalk costs him mana — each wave he farms late is a wave that outscales you.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to stacked Riftwalks — Void Stone blunts your all-magic kit and a 2-second blink outruns a 275-range taunt.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.
edits.after: Q the contact, walk him into the tornado, E in and W-taunt on landing — Null Sphere shields magic, so bait it out before your damage lands.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.

edits.before: Ahead, tax both maps: zone Kassadin with taunt threat, keep the wave middle, and R every skirmish — fed Galio makes the enemy jungler unemployed.
edits.after: Ahead, attack his mana bar: repeat Riftwalks cost escalating mana, so deny the wave, take plates, and make him blink out with nothing to farm on return.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Check it before every step-up. - W Shield of Durand is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1, but each recast in a short window costs escalating mana — punish the second blink, not the first. - Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and needs charges; once he spends it you have 21 seconds of free taunt threat at 275 range.

edits.before: Shield-trade the contacts and taunt the over-steps — your lane is a toll booth for magic damage.
edits.after: Void Stone cuts the magic your whole kit deals — win this lane on waves and plates, not on trades.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared middle wave that keeps your R timer flexible — Galio waves are about being free to leave. Worst wave: a hard-shoved wave when your bot lane is fighting — the R you couldn't channel is the fight your team lost. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.
edits.after: Best wave: a hard shove that pins him under tower — Riftwalk costs 40 mana plus escalation, so make him pick between farming and leaving. Worst wave: a wave sat near his tower, where he farms free and every level moves the game toward his side. Crash timing: crash before you recall, so the wave is gone by the time Force Pulse is back up.

edits.before: Good trade: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield. Bad trade: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.

Bad trade: Charging W at 275 range while Riftwalk is up — the charge slows you, he blinks 500 units clear, and the taunt releases onto empty ground.

edits.before: Level 3 taunt rotations tax commits; level 6 makes you a map event; first item turns AP lanes into subscriptions.
edits.after: Level 3 taunt rotations tax his step-ups; level 6 makes you a map event; his spike is rank 3 Riftwalk at 2 seconds.

edits.before: If Kassadin gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Riftwalk extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through taunt peel and R arrivals.
edits.after: If Kassadin gets a kill he buys the levels he needs, so stop dueling and take the map: shove, roam, and make other lanes pay for the time he spends farming. Every minute the game stays even is a minute he is winning.

edits.before: Carry through arrivals — Hero's Entrance turns every losing skirmish your team starts into a 5v4 with a knockup.
edits.after: Carry through arrivals — Null Sphere interrupts channels, so start Hero's Entrance from fog or after he has spent his Q.

edits.before: You are the anti-dive: taunt their engage off your carry, shield the magic, and R the flank their comp built around.
edits.after: Late Kassadin blinks every two seconds and Void Stone eats your magic — your R has to land on his target, not on him.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: He blinks 500 units on a 5s Riftwalk — hold the charge till he lands, then release inside 275.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.

edits.before: Hold E as the gap answer vs AD kits
edits.after: Hold E for his blink, not for poke

edits.before: Kassadin spends Riftwalk early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.

edits.before: That is Kassadin’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.

edits.after: Once Riftwalk reaches rank 3 and a 2-second cooldown, he becomes a split-push and pick threat who crosses 500 units onto squishies faster than you can peel, flipping the late-game power balance.

edits.before: The matchup flips once he stacks enough Riftwalks to shred your magic resist and drop his ultimate's cooldown to near-zero — at that point he can blink onto backline targets faster than you can peel or engage, and picks you off in skirmishes. Your job is to end the game before this late-game window opens, using your early lead to force objectives and close it out before he hits his full power spike.
edits.after: The matchup flips once Riftwalk reaches rank 3 and blinks on a 2-second cooldown — at that point he crosses 500 units to a backline target faster than you can peel or land a 275-range taunt, and picks you off in skirmishes. Your job is to end before that window opens, using the early lead to force objectives and close it out while his mana bar still limits how often he can chain blinks.

notes: The 'channel-interruptible' entry in missingInteractions for this matchup is WRONG and I did not write it: Null Sphere interrupts channels, it is not itself a channel — the derived flag misparsed Riot's phrase. The real interaction is the reverse and I recorded it (his Q can interrupt your Hero's Entrance channel). Existing text credited Kassadin with 'MR shred' in four places; nothing in his kit does that, so all four were corrected. packet suspectName 'Your Hero's Entrance' is a false positive. No report[] entries were edited — none were lint-flagged or carried a fabricated ability name, so they stayed out of scope per the sweep rule, though report[5].t is still generic filler.
